entities.summary:
The 2017 Oaxaca and Chiapas Earthquake was a devastating seismic event that struck the Mexican states of Oaxaca and Chiapas on September 7, 2017. With a magnitude of 8.2, it was one of the strongest earthquakes to hit Mexico in recent history. The epicenter of the quake was located in the Soconusco region of Chiapas, and it caused widespread destruction and loss of life in the affected areas.

The earthquake occurred at a time when the region was already vulnerable to natural disasters, and it had a significant impact on the local communities. Many homes and buildings were damaged or destroyed, and there were reports of landslides and power outages. The quake also caused significant damage to infrastructure, including roads and bridges.

The aftermath of the earthquake was marked by a significant response from emergency services and aid organizations. The Mexican government declared a state of emergency in the affected areas, and international aid poured in to support the relief efforts. The earthquake was a major disaster that had a lasting impact on the region and its people.

One of the most striking statistics to emerge from the earthquake was the number of people displaced by the disaster. According to reports, over 300,000 people were forced to flee their homes in the aftermath of the quake, and many of them were left without access to basic necessities like food and shelter.
